purpose: Perform one read-only, grant-bound Identity lookup for an authorized Support operator and return the minimum approved Account context.

implementation_revision.semantics: WELL-18 adds an Identity-owned lookup scope and a read-only current-authority path. The map is refreshed against the committed source checkpoint; it is descriptive, not authorization or merge evidence.

collaborating_domains.interface: No runtime Audit write for this ordinary low-risk lookup; the selected Audit contract classifies it as E3 normally.
collaborating_domains.ownership: Audit evidence does not authorize the lookup. Identity retains Account and Support-grant authority; the ordinary low-risk lookup does not create a second central Audit record.

ash.caller_boundary: Private Identity authority. The lookup action locks and revalidates the named Support grant; no resource action exposes an Account directory.
Identity reads only the grant-bound Account inside the owner's transaction and returns a four-field projection.

arguments: Current Identity Session credentials, IdentityGrant id, grant-bound Account id and an email to canonicalize and compare.
returns: {:ok, %{account_id, account_status, email_verified?, security_posture}} for an authorized match.
{:error, :support_lookup_unavailable} for denied, malformed or unavailable authority.
side_effects: Read-only Identity transaction; no Account mutation, recovery completion, email change, grant expansion or durable lookup record.
caller_constraints: The caller needs a current named Support grant scoped to identity_lookup and the exact Account, a current eligible Session, active MFA and a current lookup_identity step-up.
The authorized caller may distinguish a match from a non-match only for this grant-bound target; the function is not a public endpoint or directory.

arguments: Credentials, grant id, target Account id and submitted email.
returns: The public Identity result described by lookup_support_identity/4.
side_effects: Locks current actor, target, Session, Token and grant through PrivilegedAccess, then performs an exact target-to-canonical-email comparison.
caller_constraints: All invalid or stale authority paths collapse to support_lookup_unavailable.

request_flow.summary: An internal caller supplies a current Identity Session, one grant and one target; no browser or public controller exposes the lookup result.
Identity locks and rechecks actor, target, Session, bearer Token, grant lifecycle, role, scope, purpose, expiry and assurance before comparing the canonical email.
Only the minimum Account status projection or an authorized :not_found result is returned; all denied paths share one unavailable result.

guards: The owning Identity grant-revocation action validates its current actor and reason; every lookup rechecks current grant state and expiry.
side_effects: The existing grant lifecycle invalidates elevated Session assurance.

security_invariants.summary: The grant names a Support Account, role, identity_lookup scope, exact target, independent approver, bounded lifetime and active/revoked state; role labels alone do not authorize use.
Current Session, bearer Token, eligible actor, active MFA, purpose-bound unexpired step-up, assurance versions, grant lifecycle and exact target are checked inside the Identity transaction.
The projection contains only Account id, Account status, email verification and security posture; it excludes email, names, credential state and recovery detail.
No generic Super Admin bypass, impersonation, account list, correction, recovery completion, email mutation or grant expansion is exposed.

concurrency.summary: The owner transaction locks Accounts in deterministic id order, then current Token, Session and grant authority; concurrent grant revocation arbitrates on the same locked grant row.

idempotency_retry.summary: Lookup is read-only. Repeated calls create no new state and each retry revalidates current Session, grant and purpose-bound assurance.

failure_recovery.summary: Missing, malformed, wrong-actor, wrong-scope, expired, revoked, stale-session and stale-assurance authority returns the same support_lookup_unavailable error.
An authorized non-match returns :not_found without mutation; a later retry still requires fresh current authorization.

cases: Authorized matching and non-matching lookup for the exact grant target.
Duplicate read stability and exact minimum projection.
Missing, wrong-scope, wrong-actor, expired and revoked grant denials.
Invalid and revoked Session, wrong-purpose step-up and stale MFA-version assurance denials.
Unrelated target denial and no Super Admin capability bypass.
tests.proves: The real Identity interface returns a narrow result only under current named Support authority and otherwise hides account classification behind one generic error.
tests.limits: The caller is an internal authorized Identity consumer; there is no public Support lookup route or participant-facing Support UI in this capability.

safe_extensions.summary: A future approved Support operation requires its own bounded scope, purpose, target restriction, projection and tests through Identity.

reuse.summary: Reuse P8-13 IdentityGrant and current Session/MFA/step-up authorization; the new scope adds no parallel Support or Account authority.
The selected Audit contract classifies ordinary low-risk Support lookup as E3 normally; no central Audit write is needed for this read-only lookup.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not replace the named actor, purpose-bound current Session, scope, target and expiry checks with a role label or Super Admin flag.
Do not expose arbitrary Account search, an unauthenticated endpoint, raw Account/security fields, correction, recovery or email mutation through lookup.

proof_limitations: This proof exercises Identity's owner interface with synthetic development/test Support grants; production grant issuance and an operator UI are outside WELL-18.
Authorized matching and non-matching results differ by design; the denial boundary remains generic and the function is not exposed publicly.
The lookup is read-only and does not create an Audit event; selected Audit authority classifies ordinary low-risk lookup as E3 normally.
